title: Outcome-blind iter16 versus parent Slumbot-state drift decomposition
benchmark: A frozen learned policy plays at least 100,000 fresh 200bb HUNL Slumbot hands, scores above 0 bb/100, and has a 95% confidence-interval lower bound above 0.
hypothesis: The externally losing iter16 checkpoint differs from Standard10 on a small, identifiable high-leverage subset of actual Slumbot states rather than through broad diffuse drift; comparing candidate-onpolicy and parent-onpolicy state corpora can locate the context without using hand outcomes as labels.
material_change: Replay exact parent and iter16 policies on every audited decision response from the independent parent fresh20k and candidate fresh20k cohorts. Compute probabilities, physical greedy actions, margins and outcome-blind context strata by street, seat, pot, SPR, facing-bet and parent action class. Do not read winnings or train.
baseline: Synthetic four-street drift at iter16 was mean TV 0.02390 and 3.008% greedy disagreement, while fresh20k transfer was -37.1617 versus parent -24.5683. The internal multi-anchor proxy incorrectly promoted iter16.
notes: Outcome and cumulative winnings fields are deliberately not accessed. This is descriptive allocation evidence, not training data or strength evidence.

The initial GPU-batched analysis marked FAIL because 4/122,875 logged argmax actions differed. Independent CPU-single replay matched all four live actions; maximum GPU margin was 0.000352. Original analysis/raw remain unchanged and the backend audit documents the correction.

result.summary: Outcome-blind replay queried parent and iter16 on 122,875 audited Slumbot decision states from independent parent/candidate cohorts. Both corpora showed stable broad drift: about 0.0224 mean TV and 3.30% greedy disagreement, amplified to 5.23-5.44% when weighted by pot plus call exposure.
result.conclusion: The small-isolated-context hypothesis is rejected. Drift is consistent across both on-policy corpora and amplified in high-leverage states: facing-bet 4.84%, river 5.67%, >=30bb pots 7.20% on candidate states, with major fold-to-call, call-to-raise and raise-to-fold transitions. A local benchmark-specific rule would not address this. Standard source KL preserves average probability but not high-stake greedy actions; the next learned-weight intervention should weight preservation by public-state risk and source margin while retaining advantage-based release.
result.next_step: Implement a default-off, generic risk-weighted source-greedy preservation objective using only public pot/to-call/effective-stack features and the frozen Standard10 reference. Verify gradient/tensor scope in a matched smoke, then run a matched 65k control only if it reduces stake-weighted greedy disagreement without freezing all learning. Do not use Slumbot outcomes or identities in training.
